dedupe_keys.name: machine learning models of wildfire evacuation decisions from the 2019 kincade fire survey r code for xu et al fire technology 2023

description: This repository holds the R code for a 2023 Fire Technology paper by Ningzhe Xu, Ruggiero Lovreglio, Erica Kuligowski, Thomas Cova, Daniel Nilsson and Xilei Zhao on predicting whether households evacuate from a wildfire. Using a survey of residents after the 2019 Kincade Fire, it compares machine learning methods, run with the R libraries for decision trees, random forests, nearest neighbours, support vector machines, gradient boosting and neural networks, with logistic regression and tests whether the differences in performance are significant. The 31 survey variables describe residence and housing, warnings and who sent them, fire cues, household members and animals, emergency plans, medical conditions, age, education, income and risk perception. The code is free to download from GitHub under the MIT licence. Caveats: the survey data cannot be released under the ethics approval, so only a five-row simulated demo file is included, and the models describe one fire. Coverage is one wildfire, the 2019 Kincade Fire. Simulation uses: decision rules for households in agent-based wildfire evacuation and traffic models used by emergency services. Related records: the 2018 Camp Fire case study (case_study-camp-fire-2018-notification-evacuation) documents notification and evacuation in another wildfire.
inputs: Household survey variables: residence, housing type, warnings and their sources, fire cues, household composition, animals, emergency plan, medical conditions, age, education, income, risk perception
name: Machine learning models of wildfire evacuation decisions from the 2019 Kincade Fire survey (R code for Xu et al., Fire Technology 2023)
outputs: Predicted evacuate or stay decisions and comparison of machine learning models with logistic regression
provider: Ningzhe Xu, Ruggiero Lovreglio, Erica Kuligowski, Thomas Cova, Daniel Nilsson, Xilei Zhao
runs_on: R 3.6.1 (randomForest, tree, class, e1071, xgboost, nnet)

sources.note: README read in memory: implementation by Ningzhe Xu of 'Predicting and Assessing Wildfire Evacuation Decision-Making Using Machine Learning: Findings from the 2019 Kincade Fire' (Xu, Lovreglio, Kuligowski, Cova, Nilsson, Zhao, Fire Technology 2023, doi 10.1007/s10694-023-01363-1); R 3.6.1 with randomForest, tree, class, e1071, xgboost, nnet; wildfire evacuation.R compares machine learning models with logistic regression and tests significance; original data have 31 variables (listed) and cannot be publicly released under IRB rules; demo.csv with 5 simulated observations; LICENSE MIT (2022, EvacuationBehavior)
